examples.text: У меня один брат.
examples.trans: I have one brother.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'second', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Парни, ладно, подождите здесь одну секунду!
examples.trans: Guys, all right, wait here for one second!

examples.text: Секунду. Сейчас я позвоню.
examples.trans: One second. I'll call right now.

examples.text: Подождите одну секунду.
examples.trans: Wait one second.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('I') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Я хочу, чтобы он от нас съехал.
examples.trans: I want him to move out of our place.

examples.text: Вика, я обещаю, он скоро съедет.
examples.trans: Vika, I promise he will move out soon.

examples.text: Ты обещал мне носки не разбрасывать.
examples.trans: You promised me not to scatter your socks.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.

examples.text: Вика, это просто маленькое недоразумение.
examples.trans: Vika, this is just a small misunderstanding.

examples.text: Работа на кухне просто становится адом.
examples.trans: Work in the kitchen is simply becoming hell.

examples.text: Я просто очень сдержанный и серьёзный повар.
examples.trans: I am simply a very reserved and serious cook.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я хочу, чтобы он от нас съехал.
examples.trans: I want him to move out of our place.

examples.text: Я хотел поговорить с вами лично.
examples.trans: I wanted to talk with you in person.

examples.text: Вы хотите стать моим новым су-шефом?
examples.trans: You want to become my new sous-chef?

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to speak', forming an aspectual pair with 'сказать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Я просто не хотел говорить до вечера.
examples.trans: I simply did not want to tell you until evening.

examples.text: Зачем говорить, ведь вас бы сразу уволили.
examples.trans: Why say anything, after all they would have fired you right away.

examples.text: Это то, что ты говорил.
examples.trans: That's what you said.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Я просто не хотел говорить до вечера.
examples.trans: I simply did not want to tell you until evening.

examples.text: До свидания!
examples.trans: Goodbye!

examples.text: До завтра!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'evening', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я просто не хотел говорить до вечера.
examples.trans: I simply did not want to tell you until evening.

examples.text: Добрый вечер!
examples.trans: Good evening!

examples.text: Я позвоню вечером.
examples.trans: I'll call in the evening.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Мне мама сегодня прислала эти деньги.
examples.trans: My mom sent me this money today.

examples.text: А ещё я сегодня вас штрафую!
examples.trans: And furthermore, I am fining you today!

examples.text: Умоляю, только не увольняйте меня сегодня!
examples.trans: I beg you, just do not fire me today!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (root 'бить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to out'.

examples.text: Я уже сегодня выбил у Германа премию!
examples.trans: I already got a bonus out of German today!

examples.text: Ничто так хорошо не сближает нашу команду.
examples.trans: Nothing brings our team together so well.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'bonus', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я уже сегодня выбил у Германа премию!
examples.trans: I already got a bonus out of German today!

examples.text: Вам положена государственная премия.
examples.trans: You are due a state bonus.

examples.text: В конце года работники получили премию.
examples.trans: At the end of the year the workers received a bonus.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот так тебе будет теперь, Лёва.
examples.trans: That is what you are going to get now, Lyova.

examples.text: Вот его заявление по собственному желанию.
examples.trans: Here is his letter of voluntary resignation.

examples.text: А вот и наш камчатский королевский краб!
examples.trans: And here is our Kamchatka royal crab!

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович сейчас ваш прямой подчинённый.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich is now your direct subordinate.

examples.text: Уважаемые коллеги, прошу минуточку вашего внимания!
examples.trans: Dear colleagues, I ask for a minute of your attention!

examples.text: Да, теперь я ваш новый начальник.
examples.trans: Yes, now I am your new boss.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'money', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Интересно, а где ты взял деньги?
examples.trans: Interesting, and where did you get the money?

examples.text: Мне мама сегодня прислала эти деньги.
examples.trans: My mom sent me this money today.

examples.text: В метро деньги ещё незаметнее вытащат.
examples.trans: On the metro they will steal the money even more unnoticeably.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'лучить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to get', forming an aspectual pair with 'получать'.

examples.text: Вот ваши деньги, получите и распишитесь.
examples.trans: Here is your money, take it and sign for it.

examples.text: Кто получит деньги?
examples.trans: Who will get the money?

examples.text: Я получила письмо.
examples.trans: I got a letter.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (root 'писаться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to sign', forming an aspectual pair with 'расписываться'.

examples.text: Вот ваши деньги, получите и распишитесь.
examples.trans: Here is your money, take it and sign for it.

examples.text: Вот в ведомости расписаться надо.
examples.trans: Here, you need to sign the payment sheet.

examples.text: Распишитесь здесь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Sign here, please.
